national under-20 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Marko Gudurić''' ({{lang-sr-cyr|Марко Гудурић}}, born March 8, 1995) is a Serbian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Olimpia Milano]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He also represents the senior [[Serbia national basketball team|Serbian national basketball team]] internationally. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=6}}, he plays at the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. ==Professional career== ===Crvena zvezda (2013–2017)=== Gudurić grew up with [[KK Crvena zvezda (youth)|Crvena zvezda youth teams]] and signed his first professional contract in April 2013.{{cite web|title=Profesionalni ugovor i Marku Guduriću|url=http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/index.php/article/profesionalni-ugovor-i-marku-guduricu|publisher=kkcrvenazvezda.rs|date=April 3, 2013|language=sr|access-date=March 2, 2015|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630081158/http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/index.php/article/profesionalni-ugovor-i-marku-guduricu|url-status=dead}} He played two seasons for the Crvena zvezda development team [[KK FMP|FMP]]. On September 30, 2015, Gudurić re-signed for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] to a four-year deal.{{cite news|title=Gudurić produžio ugovor sa Crvenom zvezdom|url=https://sport.blic.rs/Kosarka/Domaca-kosarka-i-ABA/280308/Guduric-produzio-ugovor-sa-Crvenom-zvezdom|access-date=September 30, 2015|work=Blic|agency=Tanjug|date=September 30, 2015|language=sr}}{{cite news|title=Radonjić: Cilj titula, pratimo situaciju u SAD|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=09&dd=30&nav_id=1045701|access-date=September 30, 2015|work=b92.net|date=September 30, 2015|language=sr}} On October 15, 2015, he made his [[EuroLeague]] debut against [[SIG Basket]] with 6 points, 4 assists, 3 rebounds and 4 steals. One of his best moments was against [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] when he had a crucial dunk to get [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] four-point lead one minute before the end of the game on November 27, 2015. On December 18, 2015, [[KK Crvena zvezda|Zvezda]] played a game against [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] for qualifying in TOP 16 of [[EuroLeague]], Gudurić made some unconventional three-pointers and had 16 points in an amazing comeback win in front of raucous atmosphere in [[Pionir Hall]]. On July 5, 2016, he made a three-point [[buzzer-beater]] against their biggest rival [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] in Game 2 of [[Basketball League of Serbia|KLS]] Finals to secure Zvezda 2–0 lead and final result 86–87. Gudurić started his sophomore season in [[EuroLeague]] great with 21 points, 5 assists, and 4 rebounds to provide a win versus [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona Lassa]] in Round 3. ===Fenerbahçe (2017–2019)=== On July 14, 2017, Gudurić signed a four-year contract with Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]].{{cite news|title=Champs add Guduric on long-term contract|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7xybslmn9y6axfyj|access-date=July 14, 2017|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 14, 2017}} In the [[2017–18 EuroLeague]], Fenerbahçe made it to the [[2018 EuroLeague Final Four]], its fourth consecutive Final Four appearance. Eventually, they lost to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] with 80–85 in the final game.{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is 2018 EuroLeague champion|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=260&seasoncode=E2017#!report|access-date=May 20, 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=May 20, 2018}} Over 36 EuroLeague games, he averaged 6.7 points, 1.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game, while also having very high shooting percentages. In the [[2018–19 EuroLeague]] season, Gudurić was among the most valuable roster pieces that brought Fenerbahçe to their fifth consecutive Final Four appearance. However, at the [[2019 EuroLeague Final Four]], Fenerbahçe lost in the semifinal game to their arch-rivals [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] and later again in the third-place game to Real Madrid.{{cite news |last=Erel |first=Fatih |title=Real Madrid claim 3rd place in Turkish Airlines EuroLeague |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/real-madrid-claim-3rd-place-in-turkish-airlines-euroleague/1482225 |access-date=July 1, 2019 |work=aa.com.tr |date=May 19, 2019}} Over the season, Gudurić averaged career-high 9.4 points and 2.2 assists per game while shooting 47.7% from three-point territory. In the end of the season, Fenerbahçe lost the [[2018–19 Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish League]] championship after being defeated with 4–3 in the finals of [[2019 BSL Playoffs]] to Anadolu Efes.{{cite news |title=Anadolu Efes win Turkish basketball league title |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/anadolu-efes-win-turkish-basketball-league-title-144384 |access-date=July 1, 2019 |work=Hürriyet Daily News |date=June 22, 2019}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2019–2020)=== On July 31, 2019, Gudurić signed a multi-year contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[NBA]].{{cite news|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Marko Gudurić to multi-year contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-marko-guduri-to-multi-year-contract-190731|access-date=July 31, 2019|publisher=NBA|date=July 31, 2019}} On October 23, 2019, Gudurić made his debut in NBA, coming off from the bench in a 101–120 loss to the [[Miami Heat]] with nine points, two rebounds and two assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160629|title=Butler misses Miami debut, Heat beat Grizzlies 120–101|date=October 23, 2019|publisher=ESPN|access-date=October 23, 2019}} On January 30, 2020, Gudurić was suspended for one game without pay for leaving the bench during an altercation between the Grizzlies and the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web|title=Knicks' Payton, Grizzlies' Guduric and Jackson Jr. suspended; Knicks' Morris Sr. and Grizzlies' Crowder fined|url=https://pr.nba.com/new-yorks-payton-memphis-guduric-and-jackson-jr-suspended-new-yorks-morris-sr-and-memphis-crowder-fined/|access-date=October 11, 2021|publisher=NBA|date=January 31, 2020 }} During the 2019–20 season, he appeared in 44 regular season games, averaging 3.9 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1 assist on 39.5% shooting from the field. He did not appear in a single game during the 2020–21 regular season. On December 15, 2020, the Grizzlies waived him.{{cite web |date=December 15, 2020 |title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Zhaire Smith and Bennie Boatwright |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-zhaire-smith-and-bennie-boatwright-201215 |access-date=December 15, 2020 |publisher=NBA}} ===Return to Fenerbahçe (2020–2025)=== On December 18, 2020, Gudurić signed a contract with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] until the end of the 2022–23 season.{{cite web |date=December 18, 2020 |title=Marko Guduric joins Fenerbahçe Beko |url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/news/basketbol-erkek/2020/12/marko-guduric-joins-fenerbahce-beko |access-date=December 18, 2020 |website=fenerbahce.org}} On March 4, 2023, he officially renewed his contract through 2026. On May 25, 2025, Gudurić helped Fenerbahçe to their second EuroLeague championship in [[Abu Dhabi]]. He helped the team defeat the defending champions [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] in the semi-final,{{Cite web |date=2025-05-23 |title=Fenerbahce downs Panathinaikos 82-76, advances to championship game {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/fenerbahce-downs-panathinaikos-82-76-advances-to-championship-game/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} and [[AS Monaco Basket|Monaco]] in the final with 19 points and 6 rebounds.{{Cite web |date=2025-05-25 |title=Fenerbahce crowned 2025 champion with 70-81 win over Monaco |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/fenerbahce-crowned-2025-champion-with-70-81-win-over-monaco/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} ==National team career== {{also|2017 Serbia men's EuroBasket team}} Gudurić represented [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]] at the [[EuroBasket 2017]] where they won the silver medal, after losing in the final game to [[Slovenia men's national basketball team|Slovenia]].{{cite news|title=Slovenia overcome injuries to claim historic title in Dragic's swansong|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/news/slovenia-overcome-injuries-to-claim-historic-title|access-date=September 17, 2017|work=FIBA.basketball|date=September 17, Cup Power Rankings, Volume 3 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/fiba-basketball-world-cup-power-rankings-volume-3 |access-date=September 14, 2019 |work=fiba.basketball |last=OlympicTalk |date=September 10, 2019 |title=Argentina upsets Olympic silver medalist Serbia in FIBA World Cup quarterfinals |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/olympics/news/argentina-serbia-fiba-world-cup |access-date=July 28, 2024 |work=nbcsports.com}} With wins over the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] and [[Czech Republic men's national basketball team|Czech Republic]], it finished in fifth place.{{cite news |title=Serbia defeats USA in FIBA World Cup consolation round play |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/09/12/fiba-world-cup-usa-serbia-game-recap |access-date=September 14, 2019 |publisher=NBA |date=September 12, 2019}}{{cite news |last=T. |first=P. |title=Bogdanović ponovo briljirao – Srbiji peto mesto u Kini |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kina2019/vesti.php?nav_id=1591176 |access-date=September 14, 2019 |date=September 14, 2019 |language=sr}} Gudurić averaged 5.6 points, 1.1 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 7 tournament games.
